brand.name: sonarly
brand.tagline: Your music. Your disk. Any client.
brand.sector: self-hosted music streaming and collection management

sentence.en: Sonarly indexes the music folder you already have and serves it through the OpenSubsonic API, so any Subsonic client works — and your files stay on your disk, in your folder structure, exactly where you left them.

set.name: Copper Night
set.mechanism: The listening room after midnight: the same ring and copper echo pushed deeper — a blacker ground, heavy tracked capitals — borrowing Night Sweep's drama while the copper stays the only light in the room.
set.expression_move: The copper echo dot against the deepest ground of the three, under wide tracked capitals.
set.differs_by: Against the competitors' corporate primaries this keeps A's unowned warm-dark + deep-copper territory; within the refinement round it is the dramatic register the other two deliberately refuse to be.

logo.concept: The echo mark at night: same open ring and copper dot, set against a deeper black with wide heavy capitals — playback as the lit part of a dark room.

defaults_used.why: Echo Copper is the echo dot of the brand's namesake mechanism (Sonarly = sonar), not a clay or craft cue: a small signal, never a wash, measured 28 CIE76 from Ampache's #f8ac4c — the only warm competitor primary — and much deeper (L* 52 vs 70).
The ring is the sonar ping the brand is named for, not a container: it is open (60-degree gap at 3 o'clock) and carries the echo dot at its trailing end. No competitor on the shelf uses a ring mark.

rationale.claim: A restrained dose of the round-1 Night Sweep direction per owner review: a deeper ground (#0E0B09 vs #17130E), uppercase Bricolage 700 tracked +80, and no second accent — the drama comes from depth and tracking, not from lime.
Copper on the deeper ground keeps a measured 3:1+ separation (L* 52.3 accent vs L* 3.2 ground), so the echo dot stays visible without glow effects.
The mark is identical to the other refinements by design: one master ring-and-dot across all three temperatures, so the family reads as one identity with three registers.

findings.message: light: border #e9e5e3 on background #ffffff is 1.25:1, below 3.0:1 (borders: dividers are exempt, input outlines need 3:1; WCAG 2, no rounding)
dark: link #db8342 on text #f5f3f1 is 2.59:1, below 3.0:1 (underline links in dark mode (WCAG G183: without underline a link needs 3:1 against body text); WCAG 2, no rounding)
dark: border #4a3e36 on background #0e0b09 is 1.90:1, below 3.0:1 (borders: dividers are exempt, input outlines need 3:1; WCAG 2, no rounding)
Bricolage Grotesque lacks English auxiliary/punctuation characters: Ĕ Ĭ Ŏ ĕ ĭ ŏ ʻ
findings.suggested_fix: fine if the brand never writes them (loanwords, names); else another family

findings.message: Bricolage Grotesque: I/l look alike at small sizes (IoU 0.92 at 48 px)
findings.suggested_fix: no ss/cv alternates; choose another face for small text and data

findings.message: Bricolage Grotesque: ~127 KB WOFF2 for the brief's characters (one variable file, all weights; estimate)

findings.suggested_fix: give every primitive a semantic id so edits change one element per round

findings.message: accent resolves to #9b541c (UI tone); use brand-1 for #0e0b09
findings.suggested_fix: data-color="brand-1" (or logo.colors) for the exact brand colour

findings.message: sets too alike on the axes: A–B, A–C, B–C differ by 2+ steps on fewer than 2 axes (heuristic)
every set uses at least one AI-defaults item; build one set without any
